reasons: Rule correctly applied: Section 11.3 covers only survival and a generic return-or-destroy of Confidential Information, with no transition assistance, data export or certified deletion mechanic, so an insert is the right operation for this hosting/ASP agreement.

Directionality is correct — the obligation runs from Commerce One (vendor/licensor) to Corio (our client, the customer/ASP), and covers Corio's Customers' and Software Users' data flowing through MarketSite.net.

Inserted Section 11.4 tracks the preferred position and model language: up to six (6) months of transition assistance at then-current rates, return of data in a commonly used machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and certified deletion thereafter; the 'Notwithstanding Section 11.3' lead-in sensibly prevents the existing return-or-destroy sentence from defeating the new right.
Minimal-edit discipline observed: p0098 is left verbatim and the new obligation is added as a separate paragraph in the termination section.
Comment is accurate, concise, in-voice, cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback while holding the data return and deletion certificate.
